sourceSheet: Topics; Comparison by Topic; LJOVPF by Topic

topics.title: City Human Rights Commitments and Obligations
topics.summary: Naming the City's rights and equity commitments (Housing Charter, HousingTO, Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism, ReconciliationTO)
topics.assesses: Tests whether the framework accurately names relevant City housing-rights, equity, anti-Black racism and reconciliation commitments, including the Housing Charter, HousingTO and related City action plans, and shows how they guide proposed decisions.

topics.title: Acknowledge city-led Discriminatory Housing and Planning Harms
topics.summary: Acknowledgment of municipal decisions contributing to harm and displacement
topics.assesses: Tests whether documented past discriminatory housing, zoning, redevelopment, infrastructure and other municipal decisions are identified, with the mechanism of exclusion, affected groups and consequences for housing or economic security or displacement explained. Separate acknowledgement from proposed remedies.

topics.title: Acknowledge Prior City Studies and Designations
topics.summary: Formal recognition of prior City-led studies and designations for the neighbourhood/area
topics.assesses: Tests whether relevant prior City studies, adopted plans, designations and Council directions are identified accurately and whether the framework connects neighbourhood-level priorities to applicable municipal and higher-level policy, legal powers and implementation tools. Distinguish adopted direction from a proposal or study finding.

topics.title: Acknowledge Community Organizing and Prior Plans
topics.summary: Formal recognition of prior community-led organizing, plans, and communication of priorities
topics.assesses: Tests whether prior community organizing, resident-led plans, stated priorities and lived knowledge are credited accurately and demonstrably reflected in the framework. Separate from decision-making authority over this plan.

topics.title: Acknowledge Community Origins and Migration Histories
topics.summary: How the community formed, including early settlement, migration waves, early presence of marginalized communities
topics.assesses: Tests whether settlement and migration histories, including Indigenous, Black and other historically marginalized communities, are described accurately and without erasure. Where supported by records, explain how discriminatory housing access, land-use decisions or exclusion shaped settlement and tenure patterns.

topics.title: Acknowledge Indigenous Lands, Treaties and Presence
topics.summary: Indigenous territory, treaties and continuing presence
topics.assesses: Tests whether Indigenous territories, treaties, continuing presence, relationships to land and governance are recognized accurately and connected to relevant planning/stewardship decisions. Where documented, acknowledge land dispossession and discriminatory planning impacts, without conflating Indigenous rights or sovereignty with other equity categories.

topics.title: Acknowledge Displacement Risks and Investment Pressures
topics.summary: Acknowledging displacement pressure, including who is at risk, and what investment patterns are driving it
topics.assesses: Tests whether current and foreseeable residential, commercial and cultural displacement risks are assessed at neighbourhood/plan scale, including the people and institutions most at risk and the role of public investment, redevelopment and housing/space costs in creating these risks. Identify documented disproportionate impacts, evidence gaps and the limits of available data; distinguish diagnosis from remedies.

topics.title: Acknowledge Low-Income Residents and Community Belonging
topics.summary: Recognition of low income people as part of community fabric
topics.assesses: Tests whether low-income residents, including renters and people facing exclusion, are recognized as contributors to the neighbourhood's identity, relationships and future, rather than only described as recipients of assistance.

topics.title: Complete communities - services
topics.summary: Accessible, affordable neighbourhood services and community facilities
topics.assesses: Tests whether documented local needs for childcare, schools, health and social services, libraries, recreation and other community facilities are addressed through identifiable provision, delivery locations, affordability, capacity and accessible programming. Examine delivery responsibilities and community-serving access. Do not duplicate culturally specific premises and corridors (CU-2) or the distribution of overall growth benefits (R-4).

topics.title: Safe and Affordable Everyday Mobility
topics.summary: Safe, accessible and affordable everyday mobility, prioritizing walking, wheeling, and taking transit
topics.assesses: Tests whether walking, wheeling and public transit are prioritized through accessible connected routes, safe crossings, reliable connections, manageable travel costs and practical access to work, schools, parks and community facilities; cycling connections where relevant.

topics.title: Complete communities - infrastructure
topics.summary: Physical infrastructure capacity, reliability and investment
topics.assesses: Tests whether capacity and reliability of water, wastewater, stormwater, electricity and other essential infrastructure are considered against current needs and projected growth, with required upgrades, responsible agencies, financing and timing identified.

topics.title: Community Ownership and Land Stewardship
topics.summary: Community ownership, acquisition and long-term stewardship of land and space
topics.assesses: Tests whether community, non-profit or public-interest actors have identified local opportunities and funded mechanisms to acquire, own and steward land/buildings. Look for community representation in governance, municipal and higher-level support, financing or program conditions, and durable affordability/anti-displacement protections.

topics.title: Climate Resilience and Environmental Equity
topics.summary: Climate resilience, environmental justice and tree equity
topics.assesses: Tests whether heat, flood exposure, tree canopy and shade, green space, air or environmental burdens are addressed through climate resilience and equity measures benefiting current residents, with geographically specific actions where warranted.

topics.title: Food Security and Community Food Systems
topics.summary: Food security and community control of food systems
topics.assesses: Tests whether residents can access affordable, nutritious and culturally appropriate food, supported where appropriate by local food retail, community kitchens, gardens, markets, food programs and community-led food systems or food sovereignty initiatives.

topics.title: Music, Cultural Expression and Funding
topics.summary: Music, cultural expression, including honouring knowledge holders and providing sustained cultural programming
topics.assesses: Tests whether music, artistic expression and cultural histories are sustained beyond symbolic recognition through community-led programming, knowledge-holder and youth roles, intergenerational exchange, accessible cultural facilities and dependable operating/program funding with identifiable delivery partners.

topics.title: Cultural and Community Spaces, Heritage and Corridors
topics.summary: Identify, protect and sustain cultural/community spaces, heritage places and corridors
topics.assesses: Tests whether culturally significant corridors, local institutions, community gathering spaces, heritage assets and cultural focus areas are specifically identified and, where relevant, mapped; and whether the framework provides credible protection, retention, affordable replacement, secure tenure, acquisition or stewardship, accessible use and operating support. Credit both place-based cultural geography and measures securing physical spaces, without duplicating general social-service provision (CP-3) or land-acquisition mechanisms (CP-1).

topics.title: Community-Led Planning and Implementation Funding
topics.summary: Dedicated funding for community-led planning and community-directed implementation
topics.assesses: Tests whether identifiable funding sources, amounts, duration and governance arrangements finance sustained community-led neighbourhood planning and community-directed implementation, with meaningful resident control over funding decisions. Distinguish secured appropriations from proposals, and avoid giving duplicate credit for routine City infrastructure budgets already counted under relevant physical-delivery topics.

topics.title: Implementation Targets and City Accountability
topics.summary: Measurable implementation commitments, shared City leadership and accountable delivery
topics.assesses: Tests whether implementation directions identify measurable neighbourhood outcomes, milestones, sequencing, funding dependencies and responsible City divisions, agencies and accountable leaders. Assess cross-divisional coordination, decision-making authority, escalation/corrective pathways and specific commitments, rather than treating a project list or generic City partnership as proof of accountable delivery. Public progress reporting is separately assessed under D-7.

topics.title: Resourced Indigenous, Black or other Person of Colour Community Delivery Partnerships
topics.summary: Resourced Indigenous-, Black- and other racialized-led community delivery partnerships
topics.assesses: Tests whether Indigenous, Black, or POC-led community organizations have specifically identified and resourced roles in delivery, with partnership arrangements, participation in decisions, practical support and accountability.

topics.title: Public Progress and Community Impact Reporting
topics.summary: Commitment to accessible public communication, progress tracking and corrective follow-through
topics.assesses: Tests whether progress is reported at predictable intervals through accessible local communications and a public action tracker, showing commitments, achievements, delays, accountable leads, responses to community input and corrective follow-through.

topics.title: Local Business Retention and Tenant Protection
topics.summary: Retain culturally significant businesses and protect commercial tenancy continuity
topics.assesses: Tests whether long-standing, independent and culturally significant businesses receive targeted support to remain and thrive, alongside feasible protections against commercial rent or tenure instability, construction and redevelopment disruption. Assess business impact review, technical supports, affordable lease options where lawful, relocation/transition assistance, replacement premises and re-entry opportunities; distinguish these from the quantity of affordable commercial space assessed under E-1.

topics.title: Decent Local Jobs and Training
topics.summary: Local decent jobs, hiring targets, training and community benefits
topics.assesses: Tests whether local residents gain access to decent employment through clear local hiring/apprenticeship, training and community-benefit goals, defined employer, union, nonprofit and public-sector roles, appropriate agreement or procurement conditions, fair wages/benefits and publicly reported outcomes for affected communities.

topics.title: Affordable Commercial Space Supply
topics.summary: Quantified provision and retention of affordable commercial spaces
topics.assesses: Tests whether the supply of affordable commercial premises is quantified in units/area, location, suitable sizes, rent definitions and duration, including retention or replacement of space at risk. Identify practical planning and financing tools.

topics.title: Residential Tenant Stability and Eviction Protection
topics.summary: Residential tenant security, repair without displacement and anti-eviction supports including supporting tenant associations
topics.assesses: Tests whether existing renters have measures addressing eviction or renoviction risk, rent instability, unsafe repair-related displacement and barriers to organizing or obtaining tenant support. Distinct from the quality of new supply and replacement after displacement.

topics.title: Affordable Housing Scale and Depth
topics.summary: Affordable and deeply affordable housing at a scale and depth matched to need
topics.assesses: Tests whether neighbourhood-scale affordable and deeply affordable housing targets respond to documented need by income, rent, tenure, size, accessibility and long-term affordability period. Specify credible public/nonprofit/private delivery pathways and funding or regulatory instruments, distinguishing proposed targets from approved units, secured agreements and occupied homes.

topics.title: Intergenerational and Multigenerational Housing Options
topics.summary: Housing for intergenerational households
topics.assesses: Tests whether the housing mix includes suitable and affordable options for intergenerational and multigenerational households, including appropriate unit sizes, adaptable layouts and arrangements supporting extended family living. Distinct from senior-specific supportive housing.

topics.title: Supportive Housing and Homelessness
topics.summary: Supportive housing, including emergency shelter for those experiencing homelessness
topics.assesses: Tests whether the housing and service needs of people experiencing homelessness or requiring intensive support are identified locally, and linked to accessible emergency, supportive and deeply affordable options. Identifies implementation partners, housing/health service coordination and plausible municipal/provincial funding responsibilities.

topics.title: Supportive Housing for Aging in Place
topics.summary: Seniors supportive housing, to support aging in place
topics.assesses: Tests whether older residents can age in place through accessible, affordable seniors housing, supportive services, appropriate adaptations to existing homes and suitable new housing options. Distinct from intergenerational housing mix (H-2) and general supportive housing (H-3).

topics.title: Redress and Remedies for Past Municipal Harms
topics.summary: Repair and remedy for demonstrated harms caused by past public decisions
topics.assesses: Tests whether documented harms arising from past municipal/public land-use, housing, infrastructure or redevelopment decisions are matched to specific proposed remedies, responsible institutions, participation of harmed communities, dedicated resources, timelines and follow-through. Distinguish reparation, restitution, restorative measures or compensation proposals from routine prospective relocation and return protections (R-1); do not assert a legal compensation duty without legal authority.

topics.title: Community Decision-Making and Oversight
topics.summary: Resourced resident authority over plan development, decisions and implementation oversight
topics.assesses: Tests whether affected residents and community organizations have defined, representative and resourced authority in both stages: developing the framework (setting priorities, co-designing options, reviewing proposals and influencing decisions) and overseeing implementation (reviewing outcomes, accessing information and seeking corrective action). Identify formal roles, membership and selection, paid participation, decision rules, funding, public accountability and a credible response to disagreement. Consultation alone or an advisory title without meaningful authority is insufficient.

topics.title: The Right to Remain and Return
topics.summary: Right to remain; replacement, relocation assistance and return for affected residents and businesses
topics.assesses: Tests whether the right of existing residential and commercial tenants and businesses to remain is explicitly recognized AND supported by feasible anti-displacement, replacement, relocation, transition and return arrangements if people or businesses are displaced. Identify applicable legal protections versus proposed additional programs; test who qualifies, comparability and affordability of replacement space, return/priority opportunities, institutional responsibilities and the strength of implementation commitments.

topics.title: Human Rights and Anti-Racism Assessment
topics.summary: Applied human-rights and anti-racism tests for planning and investment, including confronting anti-Black racism and anti-Indigenous racism
topics.assesses: Tests whether land-use choices and investments are examined for discriminatory effects, particularly anti-Black and anti-Indigenous racism, with affected groups, barriers, mitigation and responsible actors identified, beyond a generic human-rights lens.

topics.title: Equitable Access, Inclusion and Growth Benefits
topics.summary: Equitable growth benefits and inclusive access for marginalized, low-income and existing residents
topics.assesses: Tests whether growth and public investment deliver demonstrable benefits for marginalized, low-income and existing residents, while removing age-, disability-, language- and culture-related barriers to housing, jobs, services, public spaces and civic life. Requires both meaningful accessibility and culturally appropriate measures AND identifiable priority beneficiaries, measurable equity outcomes, accountable delivery and safeguards against displacement. General inclusion rhetoric alone is insufficient.

comparators: Mount Dennis Community for All Action Plan
St. Clair Avenue West and Bathurst Street Planning Framework
assessmentScale: 1 Not addressed | 2 Acknowledged | 3 Partially developed | 4 Substantively developed | 5 Comprehensive
